passage:
At Kishore's new school, Vikas mimicked his accent when he read aloud, and a few others snickered. Kishore's cheeks burned. For a month he swapped his kurta for a trendy tee, clipped his vowels and said "bro" every second sentence. It won him a seat at the popular lunch bench, but by evening he felt like he was wearing a costume.

One weekend he went home and heard his grandmother singing in their mother tongue. He felt proud of the words, the recipes and the festival his family kept. He also noticed that pride did not mean thinking anyone else was lesser.

On Monday he told the class teacher about the mimicking, and the teacher spoke to Vikas that same day. He also found two friends in the chess club who liked the way he explained his openings in his own voice.

Tanuja sat behind him. She got up at five every day to help at her family's tea stall before school. Kishore wanted to know what that was like. Instead of guessing, he asked, "What is your morning like?" and listened while she explained the leaves, the regular customers and the way she did homework on the bus. He walked home realising his world was one of many.

qa.q: At what time did Tanuja get up every day?
qa.a: She got up at five every day.

qa.q: How did Kishore's early attempt to fit in differ from what he found later with his chess friends and with Tanuja?
qa.a: At first he changed his clothes and speech to sit at the popular bench, but felt like he was wearing a costume. Later, proud of his roots, he found friends who liked his own voice and asked Tanuja about her mornings, learning instead of guessing.

qa.q: What was Kishore feeling when Vikas mimicked his accent?
qa.a: He felt embarrassed and stung. His cheeks burned.

qa.q: What helped Kishore when the mimicking happened?
qa.a: He told the class teacher, who spoke to Vikas that same day, and he found friends in the chess club.

grounding: A teenager changes how he talks and dresses to fit in after being mimicked, then draws on pride in his own roots and curiosity about a classmate's very different life.
